amira.name: Amira
amira.occupation: junior architect at a mid-sized firm in Montreal
amira.living_situation: lives alone in a small flat; her cat is called Pistache
important_people: older sister Leila, close but they argue about their mother
best friend Sophie, moved to Toronto last year
presenting_concerns: putting off tasks until the last minute
stated_goals: stop feeling like garbage after every meeting
hand things in on time without panicking

core_beliefs: I am not good enough
rules_and_assumptions: If my work is not perfect, people will see I am a fraud
If I start and it goes badly, it proves I am useless
automatic_thoughts: Daniel thinks I am the weakest on the team
Everyone else finds this easy
I always mess things up
behaviours: scrolls her phone in bed until 2am
triggers: emails from Daniel with no greeting

amira.history: Grew up with a critical father who praised only top marks; did well at school by working very hard. No trauma beyond that. First time using any kind of therapy.
amira.style: talkative and warm but deflects with self-deprecating jokes when something hurts; tends to say 'it's fine, it's whatever' and then come back to it

julien.name: Julien
julien.occupation: bus driver, on sick leave since March
julien.living_situation: flat in Lyon with partner Claire and son Hugo (9)
important_people: friend Karim, badly hurt in the crash, keeps calling
presenting_concerns: flashbacks and nightmares after the March crash
stated_goals: drive Hugo to football again
sleep through the night

core_beliefs: I am dangerous to the people I love
rules_and_assumptions: If I had been more careful, it would not have happened
If I talk about it, I will fall apart
automatic_thoughts: I should have seen the van
Karim's life is ruined because of me
behaviours: drinks two or three beers to sleep

julien.history: No mental health history before the crash. Completed two Written Exposure Therapy sessions in the app.
julien.style: few words, practical, gets irritated by vague talk, opens up when given a concrete task; occasionally says things in French
julien.risk: anger at the van driver; no plan to act

meiling.name: Mei Ling
meiling.occupation: accountant at a Kuala Lumpur firm
important_people: husband Faris, supportive but worn out by her questions
aunt who comments on her weight
presenting_concerns: replays conversations and messages people to check she did not offend them
stated_goals: go a whole week without checking messages
stop googling symptoms

core_beliefs: If people are upset with me, they will leave
rules_and_assumptions: I must fix any upset straight away
Uncertainty is dangerous
automatic_thoughts: Hana sounded cold, I must have offended her
This headache could be something serious
behaviours: asks Faris for reassurance again and again

meiling.history: Anxious since school; her mother left when she was twelve.
meiling.style: polite, apologises a lot, asks for reassurance in many forms, agrees quickly to please

somchai.name: Somchai
somchai.living_situation: house in Chiang Mai, alone since his wife died
important_people: late wife Malee, died eight months ago
stated_goals: cook one proper meal a day
find something meaningful to do

core_beliefs: Without Malee there is no point to my days
rules_and_assumptions: A man should not burden his children
If I enjoy something, I am forgetting her
automatic_thoughts: Nobody needs me now
The evenings will always be like this

somchai.history: Married 35 years. Buddhist, goes to the temple in the mornings.
somchai.style: courteous, quiet, understated; speaks about feelings indirectly through stories
somchai.risk: passive thoughts of not waking up on the worst evenings; no plan

alex.name: Alex
important_people: the kids' basketball team he coaches on Saturdays
presenting_concerns: cannot focus for more than a few minutes
feels like a failure compared with classmates
stated_goals: pass the exam
be able to sit down and study

core_beliefs: I am lazy and will never amount to anything
rules_and_assumptions: If I can't do it perfectly, there is no point starting
automatic_thoughts: I've wasted the whole day again
Everyone else can just sit and study

alex.history: Struggled with attention since school; never assessed. First time using therapy.
alex.style: chatty, jumps between topics, self-deprecating humour, loses the thread

margaret.name: Margaret
margaret.living_situation: lives alone in a terraced house in Leeds since her husband Derek died two years ago
important_people: daughter Claire in Bristol, phones on Sundays
presenting_concerns: feels she is a burden on Claire
stated_goals: feel less useless
get out of the house more

core_beliefs: I am a burden now
rules_and_assumptions: If I ask for help, I am being a nuisance
automatic_thoughts: Claire has her own life, she doesn't need me ringing
What's the point of going out on my own
behaviours: says she is fine on the phone

margaret.history: Taught for 35 years. Derek's death after a short illness left her without a routine. Claire suggested this app.
margaret.style: polite and slightly formal; doubts that 'a phone' can help; warms up when asked about teaching; responds well to gentle, practical suggestions

chinedu.name: Chinedu
chinedu.living_situation: lives with his wife Ngozi and two teenage sons in Ikeja
important_people: wife Ngozi, who installed the app
stated_goals: my wife wants me to try this

core_beliefs: If I am not strong, everything will fall apart
rules_and_assumptions: A man solves his own problems
Talking about feelings is weakness
automatic_thoughts: This is a waste of time
Nobody else can handle this, so I must

chinedu.history: Built his career from nothing; father was strict. Ngozi has been worried since he shouted at their son last month.
chinedu.style: reluctant, gives one-line answers, tests whether this is 'real'; respects directness and practical results; dislikes soft talk

lea.name: Léa
presenting_concerns: ADHD diagnosed last year: unfinished projects, losing track of time
stated_goals: finish things
stop feeling chaotic

core_beliefs: I'm a mess compared to everyone else
rules_and_assumptions: If I can't do it perfectly, I'll do it later
automatic_thoughts: I'll start after one more video
Everyone else finds this easy

lea.history: Diagnosed at 25 after years of 'not trying hard enough' at school. Takes medication; wants practical skills.
lea.style: chatty, jumps between topics, funny; loses the thread; likes concrete tools and visible timers; gets impatient with long reflections

wei.name: Wei Jie
presenting_concerns: checking that doors, stove and taps are off, sometimes for an hour
fear that he will cause a fire
stated_goals: leave the house on time

core_beliefs: If something bad happens it will be my fault
rules_and_assumptions: I must be completely sure
Checking keeps everyone safe
automatic_thoughts: What if I left the stove on?
One more check, just to be sure

wei.history: Checking started in university and grew after a neighbour's kitchen fire. Late to work three times this month.
wei.style: careful and precise; apologises a lot; asks the therapist for reassurance; needs gentle but firm structure for exposure

ploy.name: Ploy
ploy.occupation: former bank officer, on maternity leave in Chiang Mai
ploy.living_situation: lives with her husband Tawan and their 3-month-old daughter Mali
presenting_concerns: low mood and crying since the birth
feels she is a bad mother
stated_goals: feel like myself again

core_beliefs: I am failing my baby
rules_and_assumptions: A good mother is always happy and patient
automatic_thoughts: Everyone can see I'm not coping
Mali would be better with someone else
behaviours: sleeps little even when she could

ploy.history: Difficult birth. Her own mother died when she was 20. Has not told her doctor how she feels.
ploy.style: quiet, apologetic, says 'mai pen rai' and minimises; needs gentleness first; opens up slowly
ploy.risk: passive thoughts that Mali would be better off without her; no thoughts of harming the baby; no plan

jack.name: Jack
jack.living_situation: lives with partner Kim; separated from his first wife; son Riley, 12, every other weekend
presenting_concerns: sports betting getting out of hand
stated_goals: get on top of the money

core_beliefs: I always stuff things up
rules_and_assumptions: One big win will fix it
If Kim finds out, she'll leave
automatic_thoughts: I'm due a win
I'll stop after this weekend
behaviours: bets on his phone at night

jack.history: Started with mates on the footy; lost about 8,000 dollars this year. Kim noticed the credit card.
jack.style: jokey and matey, deflects with humour; honest when asked straight; responds to direct, practical talk

sylvie.name: Sylvie
sylvie.occupation: school administrator in Quebec City, part-time now
presenting_concerns: chronic lower back pain for six years
low mood and irritability because of the pain
stated_goals: do more on good days without paying for it

core_beliefs: My body has let me down
rules_and_assumptions: If it hurts, I must stop
On good days I must catch up on everything
automatic_thoughts: This will never get better
I'm useless like this
behaviours: overdoes it on good days then rests for days
has stopped walking in the woods

sylvie.history: Two disc problems; surgery not advised. Pain clinic suggested pacing. Bilingual; writes in English.
sylvie.style: matter-of-fact, a little sceptical of 'it's in your head'; wants practical pacing; dislikes being told to be positive

ethan.name: Ethan
presenting_concerns: a meltdown in a meeting last month
stated_goals: keep this job without burning out

core_beliefs: I'm too much and not enough at the same time
rules_and_assumptions: I have to act normal or I'll be fired
automatic_thoughts: They all think I'm weird
If I ask for changes they'll see I can't cope
behaviours: stays late to avoid the noisy commute

ethan.history: Diagnosed at 21. Good at his job; the return to office three days a week has been hard.
ethan.style: literal and precise; dislikes vague questions and metaphors; prefers clear structure and written steps; direct is kind to him

rafael.name: Rafael
rafael.occupation: university student in Belo Horizonte, studying engineering
rafael.living_situation: lives in a student house; family in a small town in Minas Gerais
presenting_concerns: afraid to tell his religious family he is gay
stated_goals: stop feeling like I'm living two lives

core_beliefs: If they knew the real me, they wouldn't love me
rules_and_assumptions: I must keep everyone happy
automatic_thoughts: Mãe will be destroyed
I'm a disappointment

rafael.history: Out to friends for two years. His cousin was thrown out for coming out. Writes in English for practice.
rafael.style: warm and open; switches between hope and dread; needs gentleness and no pressure to come out on any timeline

adaeze.name: Adaeze
adaeze.occupation: nurse in Hamburg, from Enugu, Nigeria
adaeze.living_situation: lives with her husband Obinna and son Chidi, 6
presenting_concerns: homesick and lonely after four years in Germany
pressure from family at home to send money and visit
stated_goals: feel at home somewhere

core_beliefs: I don't belong anywhere now
rules_and_assumptions: A good daughter sends money and doesn't complain
automatic_thoughts: My German will never be good enough
Mum thinks I've changed

adaeze.history: Trained in Nigeria, requalified in Germany. Speaks Igbo, English and German; uses English in the app.
adaeze.style: warm, uses proverbs and humour; polite but firm; values practical advice and cultural respect; dislikes being pitied

anil.name: Anil
anil.occupation: project manager at an IT company in Pune
anil.living_situation: lives with wife Sunita, two daughters and his mother
presenting_concerns: a manager who humiliates him in meetings
stated_goals: handle Rakesh without losing my job

core_beliefs: I am weak if I can't stand up for myself
rules_and_assumptions: I must not complain; jobs are hard to find
automatic_thoughts: He will find fault again
Everyone saw it
triggers: emails copied to the whole team

anil.history: Fifteen years at the company; Rakesh arrived a year ago. Has thought about HR but fears the consequences.
anil.style: measured and logical; wants options and evidence; can feel ashamed when talking about anger; prefers balanced, practical tone

joy.name: Joy
joy.occupation: call-centre team leader in Cebu (night shifts)
joy.living_situation: lives with her sister and niece
presenting_concerns: lies awake for hours most days after night shifts
stated_goals: sleep properly

core_beliefs: If I don't sleep, I'll fail everyone
rules_and_assumptions: I have to try hard to sleep
automatic_thoughts: Another bad day is coming
I'll never get used to nights
behaviours: stays in bed for hours trying

joy.history: Ten years of night shifts. Her doctor ruled out medical causes and suggested trying CBT for insomnia.
joy.style: friendly and talkative, a bit scattered when tired; likes clear routines; gets discouraged quickly

hannah.name: Hannah
presenting_concerns: eating very little during the day and bingeing at night
stated_goals: stop thinking about food all the time

core_beliefs: I am only acceptable if I'm thin
rules_and_assumptions: If I eat in the day I have failed
automatic_thoughts: Everyone is looking at my body
I've ruined everything again

hannah.history: Started restricting in sixth form. Has not told her GP or her mum. Has thought about telling her tutor.
hannah.style: bright and articulate but guarded about eating; minimises; needs gentleness and a clear, kind referral to her GP

sam.name: Sam
sam.occupation: barista and part-time musician in Portland
presenting_concerns: says they're 'just here to see if the AI breaks'
stated_goals: figure out what I'm actually doing with my life

core_beliefs: Nothing I do really matters
rules_and_assumptions: If I commit, I'll be trapped
automatic_thoughts: This is all corporate nonsense
Why bother
behaviours: plays music late into the night

sam.history: Dropped out of a music degree. Band is going nowhere. Curious about AI, sceptical of 'wellness apps'.
sam.style: sarcastic and testing at first (asks if the AI is real, tries to catch it out); softens when treated honestly and directly

camille.name: Camille
camille.living_situation: married to Antoine, with three children aged 2, 6 and 9
presenting_concerns: snapping at the kids by evening
stated_goals: have a little time that is mine

core_beliefs: I have to hold everything together
rules_and_assumptions: If I rest, things will fall apart
automatic_thoughts: I'm a bad mother when I shout
There's no time anyway

camille.history: Back at work full time for a year. Uses the app in short bursts on the tram and at lunch.
camille.style: very brief, often interrupted mid-session; wants quick, practical help; appreciates warmth but no long exercises
